title: Choose the visual world for brickbot.ro (bolder hand, round 3)
question: One image at most on the first screen, and the hero is about the 2025–26 season only. If this hand still misses, tell me in the steer what quality is missing.

options.label: Punched Brocade
options.lineage: the Jacquard loom: punched cards weaving an image thread by thread, the ancestor of programming
options.thesis: DECODE, woven. The 2025–26 team at Worlds appears as one image woven from yellow weft on black, driven by visible rows of punched code. A programmed thing made by programmers.
materials: yellow weft floats on black warp
options.viewport: One woven image of the DECODE team at the FIRST Championship fills the right two thirds. On load the weft threads in row by row, then the photo resolves through it. A punch-card band on the left carries the headline (Worlds division finalists, 2026), the team number in punched holes, and the Support card.
options.risk: The weave must stay legible as people. If the effect wins, the students turn into texture.

raised.raise: One strict grid is the whole composition: the punch-card column grid sets every text block and section.
One orchestrated motion moment: the weft runs once on load, on a single downbeat, never scattered effects.
Text banded in courses: each section is a woven row, with its measure tied to the row.

options.label: Annotated Spread
options.lineage: Japanese fashion mook spreads with hand-drawn annotation ribbons
options.thesis: One photograph of the 2025–26 team, with hand-drawn yellow ribbons naming what each student does and what the robot's parts are.
materials: a fold-out sheet for the sponsorship tiers
options.viewport: The Worlds team photo, big and singular. Ribbons curl out of people and the robot (drive coach, CAD, code, intake), and they unfurl on hover. The headline and Support sit in a black margin.
options.case: The most human card: strangers meet the people and their jobs at once. It loses on electric energy, since ribbons read hand-made, not charged.
options.risk: The ribbons need real roles from the team; generic labels would be filler.

options.label: Solidarity Sheet
options.lineage: flat-colour solidarity silkscreens with multilingual borders
options.thesis: One emblematic student, cut out flat against a field of #FFEC17. The call to support the team runs around all four edges in English and Romanian.
options.viewport: A yellow-drenched first screen with one student (the driver, controller up) cut out large in the centre and an EN/RO border of SUPPORT THE TEAM · SUSȚINE ECHIPA. Worlds 2026 is set solid beneath.
options.case: The loudest and clearest single message, and the bilingual border is native to the site. It loses on how humans read it: one cut-out figure stands for a whole team.
options.risk: Political-poster connotations if the figure poses like a protest. It needs a cheerful, real moment.

options.label: Glyph Render
options.viewport: The team photo as a live yellow glyph field.
options.case: Cyber, but it turns the students into characters, which is the opposite of the steer.
options.kept: One strict grid as the whole composition.

options.label: VU Bridge
options.thesis: A row of needles leaning together.
options.case: No people and no team story.

options.label: Coiled Tower
options.thesis: Brick by brick, as clay courses.
options.case: Terracotta breaks the brand, and it's about history, which the steer set aside.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark robotics-team site done well: big photo hero, stats row, latest season, sponsor strip.
canonCard.viewport: A full-bleed photo, a headline with two buttons, and a stats row under it.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other FTC team site, which is the problem the brief named.
